order_note: No predecessor: SQL 146 creates two new SECURITY DEFINER functions, aws_moov_catch_up_lock_rows(...) and aws_moov_apply_collection_leg_status(...), on the payment transfer and fee obligation schema the AWS databases already have (payment_transfers with id, tenant_id, provider, environment, provider_transfer_id, provider_status, status, leg_role, amount_cents, failure_reason, provider_metadata, completed_at and updated_at; tenant_maintenance_payments with id and status), the helpers is_platform_owner() and auth.uid(), SQL 91's aws_moov_webhook_apply_active() (SQL 91 applied in production) and role checksops; a read-only production inspect confirms them. The applying login must reach both relations as the functions' owner past RLS (definer_can_write_relations: the table owner without FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, or a superuser or BYPASSRLS): a DEFINER lock or update filtered by RLS would find no row, exactly as the catch-up's own statements do today. Expected pre-state in both environments: both functions absent (release sql146 v1, derived: 1ef789645da5ce865cbb095bea1eff6775a4bedc87251e8152f41a771e659c40). Where they already exist (a re-run) they must be owned by the applying login (functions_owned_by_login), keep their jsonb result (function_results_match) and hold no EXECUTE grant other than checksops and the owner, which the file keeps, and PUBLIC, anon, authenticated and service_role, which it revokes (function_acl_replaceable). The ACL after the apply is checksops and the owner. The API change that calls them (aws/functions/api/providers/moov-status-catch-up.mjs) needs the guarded Lambda path after this pin is applied in that environment; until then (and if the API is deployed first) the catch-up apply refuses each transfer and rolls it back, as today. No API, Lambda or SPA change is part of this pin. Adds no trigger.

intended_post_state.note: aws_moov_catch_up_lock_rows(text, text, uuid[]) and aws_moov_apply_collection_leg_status(text, text, bigint, text, text, text, timestamp with time zone), owned by checksops_admin, plpgsql, VOLATILE, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path public, pg_temp, RETURNS jsonb, EXECUTE for checksops and the owner (PUBLIC, anon, authenticated and service_role revoked). Both only in the Moov webhook apply context (aws_moov_webhook_apply_active(); 42501 otherwise). The lock: only for the platform owner (auth.uid() and is_platform_owner(); 42501 moov_catch_up_forbidden), environment production or sandbox, a transfer id, at most 50 obligation ids (22023); locks the transfer's payment_transfers rows (provider moov, that environment) and the named tenant_maintenance_payments rows FOR UPDATE in id order and returns their statuses; writes nothing. The leg writer: with a user only the platform owner (42501 moov_collection_leg_forbidden), status settled, failed or returned and an amount > 0 (22023); the one payment_transfers row of that transfer id and environment, FOR UPDATE; unknown_transfer, not_owned (a SQL 109 leg or not a tenant-collection-v2 leg) and amount_mismatch write nothing; otherwise never backwards (applied / unchanged / stale), and on applied applyBillingProviderEvent's leg UPDATE (status, provider_status, completed_at for settled, failure_reason for failed / returned, updated_at). No other function, table, column, policy, RLS setting, grant, trigger or row change. The fingerprint is releaseIntendedHash('sql146', file bytes) (scripts/deployment-guard/lib/release-sql-state.mjs): ef55e1feace25188bff4890393be472deac6cdfe64e06951e53279f12641488b.
